unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: They design and present a project that explores the challenges and solutions related to natural resources (e.g. water, air); global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources. They research the importance of conserving natural resources and protecting natural resources, analyse the effects of human activity on nature, and propose actionable steps for a more sustainable future. As part of the project, students write reports, create visual aids (such as posters or presentations), and role- play as conservationists, scientists, or environmental activists. They will simulate scenarios like addressing global problems related to natural resources, pollution, or raising awareness about sustainable practices. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 10 may know what natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 10, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in nature & global problems'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a landscape, a field, a mountain, a hill, a valley, a forest, a jungle, a desert, a river, a lake, a sea, an ocean, an earthquake, to grow, to plant, to water, to gather, to pick, to take care, to protect, to save, to recycle, to feed, to observe, to save, to collect'' and also some structures such as ''She is planting flowers in the garden. They aren’t hiking up the mountain because the weather is too dangerous. Were you cycling near the lake when the lightning struck? While we were having a picnic by the river, a sudden rainstorm began'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about global problems related to natural resources and solutions by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Solutions for Global Problems The teacher divides students into small groups and assigns each group a global problem, such as climate change or water shortage. Students discuss the problem using the target vocabulary, including terms such as ''renewable resources'', ''efficient energy use'', ''to recycle'', and ''to raise awareness'', as well as structures such as ''which, that, and so''. Each group creates a plan that explains the problem, its causes, and solutions with reasons. For example, for climate change, a group might state: ''Climate change, which is caused by greenhouse gases and overuse of fossil fuels, requires immediate action. We suggest using renewable resources, such as solar and wind energy, that are sustainable and reduce carbon emissions. To solve this, it is important to raise awareness, so people learn to save energy and recycle''. After each group presentation, the teacher provides feedback on correct use of target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective : To identify and categorise natural resources, global problems, and actions to protect the environment in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Save the Planet: Match and Share The teacher shows flashcards of natural resources such as water, forests, and animals, asks students to name them, and repeats the words. Next, s/he provides a worksheet with vocabulary words like ''solar energy'', ''pollution'', and ''to recycle'' and asks students to match them to the categories ''Natural Resources'', ''Global Problems'', and ''Protecting Natural Resources'' by drawing lines. For example, students will match ''solar energy'' to ''Natural Resources'', ''Pollution'' to ''Global Problems'', and ''To recycle'' to ''Protecting Natural Resources''. After completing the worksheet, students take turns reading aloud the words they matched in each category. The teacher listens, provides feedback, and corrects any misplacements. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
